The operational details and reports of continued compromise do."},"independent_cross_check":{"reported_facts":["Cloudflare’s February 2024 account reports that credentials stolen in the October 2023 Okta compromise were mistakenly considered unused and left unrotated; attackers later used them to access its Atlassian environment. [CF2024]"],"inference":"This independent victim account supports the bounded proposition that credentials can remain usable after the basis for trusting their use has failed. Require evidence of authorization for each business action, and verify the assumptions behind the access path and incident recovery. Previously trusted access becomes insufficient evidence when someone can reuse or reproduce it outside the conditions that justified that trust.","recommendation":"For payment approvals, retain approved-record validation, binding between validation and debit stages, second-level verification and API-stage limits. Add explicit scrutiny of shared fetcher allow-lists, non-production access to production and controls that trust the client package. After an incident, require forensic verification of eradication and continued threat hunting. CERT-In recommends these measures across its two advisories; the supplied evidence does not measure their effectiveness.
